topic: Mirror Ray Diagramming and Image Characteristics
key_concepts: Principal axis, center of curvature, vertex, focal point, radius of curvature, and focal l
The focal point is midway between the vertex and the center of curvature.
Ray diagrams use four principal rays to determine image location, size, orientation, and t
A ray parallel to the principal axis reflects through the focal point in a concave mirror.
A ray passing through the focal point reflects parallel to the principal axis.
A ray passing through the center of curvature reflects back along itself.
Concave mirrors can form real or virtual images depending on object location.
Convex mirrors produce only virtual images behind the mirror.
Convex mirror images are upright and reduced.
An object between the focal point and vertex of a concave mirror produces a virtual, erect
Real images are produced by real rays and can be projected on a screen.
Virtual images can be seen but do not really exist at the image location.
